title: Magpa- and pa- + -in verb forms
summary: Verbs for having something done by someone else: magpakáin, pakaínin (feed someone), magpabása, pabasáhin (order someone to read)
goals: Understand what magpa- and pa- + -in verbs express
Tell the active magpa- verbs from the passive pa- + -in verbs
Form all the tenses and the verbal noun for roots ending in a consonant (kain)
Form them for roots ending in a vowel, using the suffix -hin (basa)
Read the book's sample sentences and see what each one emphasises

blocks.t: The affixes [[magpa-|pred]] and [[pa- + -in|pred]] make verbs that express an **order** to be done to the subject of the verb. They suggest that **someone is giving orders to have something done to another**.

head: Tagalog
Meaning
blocks.title: Two examples from the book
blocks.note: The book prints pinakain here without an accent mark, and pinakáin in the tables below.

head: Affix
Kind of verb
rows: **passive**: the subject is the one the order is about
blocks.title: Active and passive
Not the same as i- verbs
blocks.t: In Lesson 32 you met passive **i-** verbs, which express actions done **for someone**. Magpa- and pa- + -in verbs are different: they are about **ordering** something to be done.

blocks.title: In English
blocks.t: English uses words like *have*, *make* or *order* for this idea: *to have someone read*, *made someone read*, *order someone to read*. Tagalog builds the idea into the verb itself.

blocks.title: Different shapes
items: Magpa- verbs and pa- + -in verbs form their tenses **differently**.
Pa- + -in verbs use the suffix **-hin** (instead of -in) when the root **ends in a vowel**: basa → pabasá**hin**.

blocks.title: kain → magpakáin
Spot the pattern
items: Like mag- verbs (Lesson 14), **m** changes to **n** for the past and present: **m**agpa- → **n**agpa-.
Present and future repeat **pa**, the second syllable of the prefix: nagpá**pa**káin, magpá**pa**káin.

head: Form
Tagalog
How it is made
Meaning
rows: -in- between the first and second letters of pa- + root
-in- inside pa- + first syllable of the root repeated + root
pa- + first syllable of the root repeated + root + -in
pa- becomes pagpa- + second syllable of the prefix (pa) repeated + root
blocks.title: kain → pakaínin
Spot the pattern
items: Past and present put **-in-** inside pa-: p**in**a-.
Present and future repeat the **first syllable of the root**: pinakákain, pakákainin.
Only the infinitive, imperative and future keep the **-in** suffix.
The verbal noun is the same for both kinds: **pagpapakáin**.

blocks.title: basa → pabasáhin
-in or -hin?
blocks.t: Kain ends in a consonant, so it takes **-in**: pakaín**in**. Basa ends in a vowel, so it takes **-hin**: pabasá**hin**, pabábasa**hin**.

blocks.title: Accent marks in the book
blocks.t: The tables are copied as printed. The book marks the verbal nouns differently: **pagpapakáin** for kain but **pagpápabása** for basa. It also prints **nagpápabasa** and **magpápabasa** with no mark on *basa*, while the kain forms have **nagpápakáin** and **magpápakáin**.

Lesson 31 showed how nouns are formed by putting articles before verbs and adjectives. The same can be done with magpa- and pa- + -in words. Their **verbal nouns** become quite similar to the English **-ing** (gerund) phrase, as in *__Feeding someone__ makes him happy*.
Each pair says nearly the same thing, once with an **active** magpa- verb and once with a **passive** pa- + -in verb. The book gives a literal translation first, then a natural one.

items.tl: Nagpápabasa silá sa mga páaralán ng mga aklát ni Rizal.
items.en: They order the books of Rizal read in schools. (literal: They order to be read in schools the books of Rizal.)

items.tl: Pinabábasa sa mga páaralán ang mga aklát ni Rizal.
items.en: The books of Rizal are ordered read in schools. (literal: Are ordered read in schools the books of Rizal.)

items.tl: Nagpakáin kamí ng mahihírap na táo.
items.en: We fed the poor. (literal: Were fed by us the poor people.)

items.tl: Pinakáin namín ang mahihírap na táo.
items.en: The poor people were fed by us. (literal: Gave food by us the poor people.)

blocks.title: Same meaning, different focus
items: The translations are similar, but the **first** sentence emphasises the **giving of food** by the subject (namín).
The **second** sentence emphasises the **receiver** of the action (mahihírap na táo).

items.en: He/She had a haircut. (literal: He/She ordered his/her hair cut.)
He/She had a haircut. (literal: Had cut his/her hair.)

blocks.title: Spellings in the book
blocks.t: The book prints **namín** in these sentences; Lesson 8 printed it as **námin**. It also prints **Nagpagupít** (with a mark) but **Pinagupit** (without). The sentences are copied as printed.

The book ends with practice: change active sentences into passive ones, change passive sentences into active ones, and give ten other magpa- and pa- + -in verbs. It does not print the answers, so here you can practise **spotting** which kind each sentence uses.

head: Sentence
Kind of verb
rows: Ang áking katúlong ay **nagpakáin** ng batà.
**Nagpápabasa** ang aming gurò ng páhayagan áraw-áraw.
**Nagpalínis** ako ng silíd sa páaralán sa mga batà.
**Nagpápagamót** ng sakít ang matandáng babáe sa doktór.
**Nagpaalís** ng mga batà sa kanyáng hardín ang matandáng laláki.
blocks.title: Change into passive sentences

head: Sentence
Kind of verb
rows: **Pinakuha** ko ang aklát sa batà sa aklátan.
**Pinaayos** ko ang áking silíd sa áming katúlong.
**Pakukunin** ko ng pera sa bangko ang áking asawa.
blocks.title: Change into active sentences
Clues
items: **nagpa-** at the start = active magpa- verb (past or present).
**pina-** at the start = passive pa- + -in verb (past or present).
**pa-** with **-in** at the end = passive pa- + -in verb (infinitive, imperative or future).

blocks.title: Remember
items: magpa- = active; pa- + -in (variant pa- + -an) = passive. Both are about ordering something to be done to another.
Active past and present change magpa- to nagpa-; present and future repeat pa: nagpápakáin, magpápakáin.
Passive past and present put -in- inside pa-: pinakáin, pinakákain.
Roots ending in a vowel take -hin: pabasáhin, pabábasahin.
Verbal nouns start with pagpa- and work like English -ing phrases.

vocab.note: Verbal noun of both magpakáin and pakaínin
Passive pa- + -in verb; also the imperative: Feed someone.
The tables also give: to have someone read
Verbal noun of both magpabása and pabasáhin
Passive; takes -hin because basa ends in a vowel
Literally: ordered (his/her) hair cut. Nagpagupít siyá ng (kanyáng) buhók.
Pinagupit niyá ang kanyáng buhók. He/She had a haircut.

exercises.q: What do magpa- and pa- + -in verbs suggest?
options: Someone is giving orders to have something done to another
Someone is doing something for another person
Someone is able to do something
exercises.answer: Someone is giving orders to have something done to another
exercises.explain: For example, magpakáin = to feed someone.

exercises.q: Magpa- verbs are…
exercises.explain: Pa- + -in and its variant pa- + -an are passive.

exercises.q: What is the variant of pa- + -in?
exercises.explain: Pa- + -in and pa- + -an verbs are passive.

exercises.q: Which passive verbs express actions done FOR someone?
exercises.explain: Magpa- and pa- + -in verbs differ from i- verbs (Lesson 32).

exercises.q: When do pa- + -in verbs use the suffix -hin?
options: When the root ends in a vowel
When the root ends in a consonant
exercises.answer: When the root ends in a vowel
exercises.explain: basa → pabasáhin.

exercises.q: What is the past tense of magpakáin?
exercises.explain: magpa- becomes nagpa- + root.

exercises.q: What is the present tense of magpakáin?
exercises.explain: nagpa- + pa repeated + root: feeds someone.

exercises.q: What is the future tense of magpabása?
exercises.explain: magpa- + pa repeated + root: will have someone read.

exercises.q: What is the past tense of pakaínin?
exercises.explain: -in- goes between the first and second letters of pa-: was/were fed.

exercises.q: "Pakákainin" means…
exercises.explain: pa- + first syllable of the root repeated + root + -in.

exercises.q: Which is the passive infinitive of basa?
exercises.explain: pa- + root + -hin: to order someone to read.

exercises.q: "Pinabábasa" is which tense?
exercises.explain: pinabábasa = making someone read.

exercises.q: Verbal nouns of these verbs begin with…
exercises.explain: pagpapakáin (feeding someone), pagpápabása (having someone read).

exercises.q: A verbal noun such as pagpapakáin is quite similar to…
exercises.explain: Feeding someone makes him happy.

exercises.q: "Nagpakáin kamí ng mahihírap na táo" means…
exercises.explain: Nagpakáin is the past of magpakáin.

exercises.q: Which sentence emphasises the RECEIVER of the action (the poor people)?
options: Pinakáin namín ang mahihírap na táo.
Nagpakáin kamí ng mahihírap na táo.
exercises.answer: Pinakáin namín ang mahihírap na táo.
exercises.explain: The passive sentence emphasises mahihírap na táo.

exercises.q: "Pinagupit niyá ang kanyáng buhók" means…
exercises.explain: Literally: Had cut his/her hair.

exercises.q: In "Pinakuha ko ang aklát sa batà sa aklátan", the verb is…
exercises.explain: The book asks you to change it into an active sentence.

exercises.q: In "Nagpalínis ako ng silíd sa páaralán sa mga batà", the verb is…
exercises.explain: The book asks you to change it into a passive sentence.

exercises.q: Which of these is an ACTIVE magpa- verb?
exercises.explain: nagpa- at the start is active; pina- and pa- … -in are passive.

recap: Magpa- (active) and pa- + -in (passive, variant pa- + -an) verbs express ordering something to be done to another.
kain: magpakáin, nagpakáin, nagpápakáin, magpápakáin; pakaínin, pinakáin, pinakákain, pakákainin.
basa (ends in a vowel, so -hin): magpabása, nagpabása, nagpápabasa, magpápabasa; pabasáhin, pinabása, pinabábasa, pabábasahin.
Verbal nouns begin with pagpa- (pagpapakáin, pagpápabása) and work like English -ing phrases.
The active sentence emphasises the giver; the passive one emphasises the receiver of the action.
